questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was incredibly important for me to choose a host university that had plenty of opportunities for international students to participate in social activities. But I also really wanted to go somewhere where I was interested in learning more about the culture and history.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really loved going on exchange and I cannot recommend it enough to anyone!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy, everything was sent to us by email.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The first few days were dedicated to orientation, and the international office sent out thorough emails detailing all the important information

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy seeing as my host university helped me out. Definitely try to contact your host university and see what offers they have and how they can help you. I stayed at Nido Broga House which was perfect for me, although a bit expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: While I lived off campus I still lived with 7 other international students who were all in the same boat as me, it was quite perfect. Besides, Cork is a very walkable city and the walk to campus from where I lived was only 10-20 minutes, depending on which building.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a bit too expensive for my budget, and I didn't like that I had to pay for laundry

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The international office sent out step by step guides via email, detailing everything you needed to know, as well as which websites you were to use and how to go about the whole thing - very easy, if a bit complicated.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an email you could contact, a phone number, and the international office was open most days of the week - they were so sweet and helpful with everything.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try out a few classes in the period where you can still switch, make sure you get your timetable sorted as quickly as possible, because some of the classes might be taught at the same time. There is a good amount of time to do this though, but I attended multiple lectures in a few different courses to figure out which ones I wanted.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really loved all the classes I had, except for one.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were incredibly interesting, taught by passionate professors who made it all the more enticing. I will say that most of the classes I took were easier than what I'm used to at UCPH, but that was perfect for a semester abroad.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was mostly the same, although at UCC I only had lectures, but it was fairly easy to get into.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
FL2012 Exploring the Otherworld: Popular Belief and Symbols
EN3015 Of Monsters and Men: Old & Early English Literature
GA2033 Language & Culture in an Irish-Speaking Area
EN3005 Introduction to Irish Literature
FL3015 Indigenous Knowledge: Herbs and Healing in Irish Folklore

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Definitely the Language & Culture one! It was a residential course an hour away from UCC and it was the best five days of my exchange stay. I met so many other international students and generally enjoyed the whole thing.

Otherwise the folklore classes are also incredibly interesting and utterly unique - the professors are really lovely too, although I cannot recommend FL3015.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Laundry! I had to pay €5 every time I washed or dryed a load, on top of an already pretty steep rent...

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were a little on the expensive side, but the pubs and restaurants were a little cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything you could imagine, from sports clubs to tea societies - there was so much to choose from

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't have much time for clubs or societies, but definitely try to make time for it! I regret not prioritising this!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Galway or Dublin for a weekendtrip, go hiking in Killarney and spend time exploring the beauty that is Co. Cork - there is so much to see! Cobh and Kinsale are both lovely towns 30 minutes away from Cork by easily accessed public transport.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the Irish are lovely people! There were so many other international students in the same boat, which was so nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular, it was a fairly similar culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pub culture was particularly amazing, everyone was so friendly and there was a lot of traditional Irish music many places.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make sure you travel around Ireland, it is far lovelier than you'd think. Try out different courses, there are so many to choose from! Go on the Language and Culture trip, you'll meet so many international students, and I've made friends for life in those 5 days.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to find some sort of accommodation with other students, it makes socialising so much easier! And as close to the town centre as possible, there's so much to experience.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many other international students, it's definitely helped me grow both personally and academically.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That I couldn't stay longer! Although there were also quite a few written assignments, but this was hardly anything to complain about.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you get the opportunity to go on exchange (especially in Ireland) DO IT! I promise you won't regret it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
